mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the person's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Executed domiciliation contract and declaration of designated registered office in Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Subject to compulsory PEP, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, and Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs sanctions screening; automated batch screening at onboarding and continuous transaction monitoring; positive match triggers the filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) and enhanced due diligence in line with FATF standards and the 4th/5th EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online e-desks and RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), accessible through www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin alphabet script, using French, German, Luxembourgish, or acceptable common-language terms; any non-Latin script name must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters and recorded in the RCS; the transliterated name is the effective legal name. The name must not be unlawful, scandalous, contrary to public policy, or misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension is available; if the reservation lapses, a new request must be filed. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the RCS/LBR within 5 business days; if rejected again, the applicant may bring administrative proceedings before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within one month of the second refusal, or upon written notice that no further administrative review will be provided.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permitted for the registered office of a SCSp provided the provider supplies a physical street address in Luxembourg, mail handling, and statutory notice receipt; the existence of a virtual office alone does not create taxable substance and may be rejected if the partnership seeks to claim treaty benefits or EU directive advantages.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a non-licensed, low-risk logistics-tech SaaS SCSp with no statutory license, the estimated annual risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the RCS or the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) is approximately 10%; the likelihood rises to around 35% if the partnership contracts with EU public authorities or asserts significant substance for tax transparency purposes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 90-1 et seq. regarding the Société en Commandite Spéciale), and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on the Annual Accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Partnership (Contrat de Société) of the SCSp, executed by notarial deed and filed with the RCS for legal publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp. No escrow account or bank capitalization certificate is statutorily required. Limited Partner contributions may be in cash or in kind and may remain uncalled unless the partnership agreement provides otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the formation deed of the SCSp be approved and adopted in its final form, including the subscription of one Partnership Interest by each Limited Partner and the acceptance of the General Partner's contribution in full accordance with the partnership agreement, such interests being fully subscribed without any minimum capital requirement. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office be fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the entity be authorized to open, operate and close bank accounts and to appoint banking signatories. RESOLVED FURTHER: That [Name] be appointed as Gérant with sole signature power and [Name] as Compliance Officer for AML/KYC duties, such appointments effective upon RCS registration and ratification by all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the Luxembourg Business Registers online portal. The requested name must include 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The registrar will verify the name against existing entities and grant priority of the name upon approval. No notarization is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Identification of the General Partner and Limited Partners
Proof of appointment of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or public policy conflict, submit an amended name reservation with revised proposed names within 5 business days. No re-filing fee is charged for a second submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Notarial Deed of Formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public appointed by the parties and admitted in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the Articles of Partnership (Contrat de Société) incorporating the terms of the SCSp, including the registered office address, purpose, contribution schedule, distribution waterfall, scope of the business, management powers of the Gérant, and provisions consistent with the SCSp's pass-through status. The deed is executed before the notary in the presence of all founding partners or their authorized attorneys-in-fact.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national ID cards of all founding partners
Power of attorney if a partner is not represented personally
Proof of address for each partner
Draft partnership agreement reviewed and approved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions in the draft, the partners will be requested to supply supplemental information and signatures. A new execution date may be set without additional penalty beyond the notary's standard rescheduling fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Formation Documents with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Filing Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the certified notarial deed and a request for registration of the SCSp with the RCS within one month of execution. The filing is made via the RCS electronic platform. The filing triggers publication in the RESA. The SCSp is legally effective from the date of signature of the deed, but filing is required for mandatory publication and third-party opposability.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed
Filing form duly completed by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query (e.g., missing annexes or inconsistent articles), the notary shall resubmit corrected documents within 15 days. Failure to cure may lead to a repeat filing fee; administrative appeal to the Registrar may be lodged within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA Electronic Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA Publication System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of RCS registration, the LBR publishes the original articles of partnership and a consolidated legal notice in the RESA. This publication is mandatory and must occur within the legal timeline. The SCSp may then request certified excerpts of the RCS registration for banking, tax, and contracting counterparties.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed beyond 5 days, contact the LBR helpline to expedite. Minor errors in the published text will be corrected by filing a submitted errata to the RCS; material errors require an amending notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of the Inaugural Partners' Meeting and Issuance of Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SCSp General Partner and Gérant (Management Body)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The General Partner convenes the initial partners' meeting or adopts written resolutions. The first board/organ resolution approves the registered office, subscribes partnership interests, appoints the Gérant and Compliance Officer, and authorizes opening bank accounts. Minutes are executed in writing and retained in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Appointment form for the Gérant and Compliance Officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner disputes the adoption, an extraordinary partner meeting shall be called within 10 days. Any irregularity in the minutes is cured by a supplemental resolution, with the original minutes annotated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Economic Stimulation (autorisation d'établissement window)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'Établissement (Business Establishment Permit) – required only for physical commercial presence, not for pure SaaS licensing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No EIA Required for software-only logistics fleet dispatch platform with no on-site industrial installations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for digital activities. If office lease has minimal HVAC, comply with Luxembourg general heating and air conditioning emission thresholds; no industrial wastewater or VOC discharge permits applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard fire safety certificate from the municipal fire service (Service d'Incendie et de Secours) for office premises; structural load inspections based on building code compliance; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labour in accordance with the Labour Code for workstation ergonomics and server room fire suppression if applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct income taxes, with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT / Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority) for value added tax; principal electronic portal is MyGuichet.lu operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the Luxembourg State IT Center.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SCSp must execute a notarial deed of limited partnership agreement, which is filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) to obtain a legal identifier (matricule / numéro d'identification national) for the SCSp. Thereafter, the SCSp, acting through its manager or registered agent, must apply separately to the AEDT for VAT registration if it makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg; for direct income tax purposes the ACD assigns a Luxembourg corporate tax reference number to the partnership and individual fiscal numbers to non-resident partners only as required for filing/withholding. Foreign entities may use an electronic registration file via MyGuichet.lu, with power-of-attorney documentation and valid passports/articles of incorporation apostilled as applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — An SCSp is fiscally transparent by mandatory legal tax characterization: it is not a separate subject of Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (IAC), or net wealth tax; profits and losses are passed through to partners and taxed at partner level. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is treated as a taxable person if it independently carries on an economic activity, and it may be registered as a VAT debtor in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. The SCSp's pass-through status is a statutory default and cannot be unilaterally converted to opaque corporate taxation; investors desiring entity-level taxation must instead use a separate corporate vehicle such as a S.à r.l. or S.A. Available elective mechanisms relevant to SCSp structures include: (i) VAT grouping election under Luxembourg VAT law allowing an SCSp to join a group of closely-linked Luxembourg taxable persons treated as a single taxable person; (ii) option to file consolidated tax returns does not exist; (iii) hybrid-mismatch management is limited to ATAD-aligned anti-abuse rules and mandatory disclosure of cross-border arrangements, with no elective deduction/income reclassification mechanism to eliminate hybrid outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) under Luxembourg Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for small enterprises established in Luxembourg under the Article 287(15) derogation; however, no threshold applies to non-established foreign suppliers or to supplies of electronically supplied services subject to reverse charge or domestic Luxembourg VAT, and once the EUR 35,000 ceiling is exceeded VAT registration is mandatory from the first day of the month following the threshold crossing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate continuous transaction controls, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or an API-based B2B e-invoicing clearance platform. Mandatory electronic invoicing exists only for B2G invoices issued to central and municipal public contracting authorities, which must be transmitted in structured electronic format (e.g. PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 or Factur-X/EN 16931) through an approved access point. For B2B and B2C invoices, paper, PDF, and EDI are accepted subject to recipient consent; all invoices must nevertheless be issued without undue delay and be retained in full for VAT audit purposes. Taxpayers filing Luxembourg VAT returns must do so electronically via MyGuichet.lu or the AEDT secure e-space, with standard monthly or quarterly VAT return obligations and annual recapitulative statements for intra-Community supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for the 0% Luxembourg VAT export exemption where the seller dispatches or transports the goods directly out of the European Union within the statutory deadline (generally within three months from delivery/supply) and holds positive documentary evidence of physical export, including a recognized EU customs export declaration and transport documents. For offshore/digital services such as fleet route optimization and cloud-based telematics SaaS, zero-rating is not normally used; instead, the place-of-supply rules apply: B2B services to a non-EU customer fall outside Luxembourg VAT (customer location rule) and B2C electronically supplied services to a non-EU resident also remain outside Luxembourg VAT. If the recipient is a taxable person holding an EU VAT identification number in another Member State, the supply is subject to reverse charge in that Member State and no Luxembourg VAT is charged; for EU consumer customers the supplier may need to register in the applicable Member State or use the OSS/IOSS regime for digital services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Exporter's electronic customs export declaration (SAD/Declaration submitted via Luxembourg Customs, Direction des Douanes et Accises, and validated under the EU Customs Decision System)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure of goods from the EU
Original commercial invoice and underlying contract or purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 / account statement showing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency from the overseas buyer
Proof of terminal/warehouse loading and delivery such as signed proof of delivery (POD) or customs transit completion documents
Any applicable export control or dual-use license issued by the Luxembourg Ministry of Economy or EU authorities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg imposes no pure exchange-control repatriation deadline, but a 180-day benchmark is commonly used by the AEDT and customs administration as the documentary window for export incidence; if export proceeds are not received or are repatriated significantly later without adequate commercial justification, the tax authorities may treat the transaction as not bona fide. Where export documentation is missing, insufficient, or fraudulent, the 0% rate is clawed back retroactively, the VAT becomes payable together with default interest at the statutory rate, and the AEDT may impose administrative penalties of up to 100% of the tax evaded (typically 10% to 20% for non-willful deficiencies) plus fines; deliberate or fraudulent fabrication of export evidence is a customs and VAT criminal offense carrying imprisonment and substantial monetary penalties, and Luxembourg anti-fraud units coordinate with OLAF for intra-EU and cross-border enforcement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank (ECB); Luxembourg maintains a fully liberalised, notification-only monetary regime with no separate central foreign-exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no Luxembourg exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements and no approval gates for capital contributions, partnership distributions, dividend-equivalent profit allocations, loan repayments or SaaS royalty receipts. Profit remittance by an SCSp to non-resident partners is unrestricted under Article 63 TFEU free movement of capital; only ordinary AML reporting and CRS/FATCA tax-transparency duties apply, with no beneficial-ownership withholding on profit distributions for a transparent partnership, unless Luxembourg withholding rules on non-resident partners are triggered by specific facts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline and no holding-period constraint on export or service proceeds. EUR and foreign-currency receivables may be retained freely in multi-currency accounts, and the logistics-fleet-dispatch SaaS may invoice global customers in USD, EUR or GBP without BCL reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (partner subscriptions) and Operational Multi-Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (Spuerkees, BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account and Collection Account
Operational Account with Treasury and FX Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for payment collection only. A CSSF-authorised Luxembourg EMI or an EU-passported EMI under PSD2 may lawfully operate as a settlement rail for low-risk SaaS receivables, including Stripe Billing via Stripe Payments Europe. However, EMIs lack deposit-guarantee coverage, cannot grant credit or commercial letters of credit, and impose treasury concentration caps. Offshore/non-EEA digital EMIs are not viable as the primary treasury rail because tier-1 Luxembourg banks will generally reject incoming settlement from unlicensed crypto-EMIs or remote, unregulated platforms, and CSSF AML/CFT guidance requires the SCSp to maintain its core liquidity at a supervised credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law and CSSF Regulation N° 12-02 do not impose a statutory requirement that directors appear physically. In practice, tier-1 banks allow fully remote onboarding for a low-risk corporate SaaS client using notarised/apostilled certified copies, a live video identification, and an introducer engaged from the Luxembourg regulated sector (notary, lawyer or bank). For SCSp partners resident in higher-risk jurisdictions or with complex source-of-wealth, a brief in-person meeting with the relationship manager or an EU-based notary may be imposed. A physical interview is the exception, not the rule, for a standard logistics-technology operating company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp with unidentified ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs) extract; executed partnership agreement (contrat de societe) with a full look-through list of all partners and UBOs above 25%; certified passports and proof of address of each UBO; CSSF-compliant organisational chart; declaration confirming no bearer shares and no nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letterbox-company indicator / absence of Luxembourg economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Local substance file: registered office lease at a genuine BCL-accepted domiciliation agent, Luxembourg payroll or payroll outsourcing agreement, local director or authorised manager mandate, board/business-plan evidencing fleet-telematics software activity, RCS extract, and professional indemnity cover evidencing real operational conduct.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth of non-resident SCSp partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters from the partners' home institutions (issued within 3 months), 6-month source-of-wealth statements, tax returns, audited financial statements of the contributing entity, sale/exit documentation for historical liquidity, and a sworn declaration on the absence of proceeds of tax offence or predicate crime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or high-risk jurisdiction footprint in partner chain or client base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions/PEP/source-of-funds questionnaire; official passport copies; proof of physical residence; corporate structure chart with jurisdiction rationales; independent professional (lawyer/accountant) reference; negative media and sanction-list screening results; commitment to transparent no-cash, no-crypto, no-gambling payment flows for the fleet logistics SaaS.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital contributions must arrive by SWIFT MT103 from each partner's own account in the partner's own name to the SCSp's capital account, never from a third-party or opaque intermediary; for EUR from EEA, use a SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (up to EUR 100,000) with beneficiary BIC (e.g., BGLLLULL for BGL BNP Paribas) and exact legal-entity name 'LU_SCSP'; for USD or non-SEPA, route via CHIPS/Fedwire correspondent with the Luxembourg bank's USD correspondent and include SWIFT field 70 remittance narrative such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO LU_SCSP / INVS / CAPITAL CALL DATE'; ISO 20022 purpose code 'INVS' (investment) is preferred, with 'OTHR' accepted as fallback; banks will require the capital-call notice, the executed partnership agreement, the RBE extract and proof that all funding partners are disclosed as UBOs before accepting high-velocity or large-volume injections; avoid repeated deposits below EUR 10,000 to prevent artificial-structuring flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU/SEPA disbursements (EUR) clear via TARGET2 using SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer; US-USD and APAC-USD flows clear via SWIFT MT103 through the bank's New York/HSBC/JPMorgan correspondents with purpose code 'SUPP' (supplier payment) or 'TRAD' (trade settlement); high-frequency payouts to remote fleet operators across emerging markets use virtual IBANs and a payment-hub overlay, retaining a full audit trail for each beneficiary; for physical telematics-device procurement, a Commercial (Documentary) Letter of Credit may be opened by the SCSp as importer, although pure SaaS subscriptions do not commercially require LCs; a standby LC or bank guarantee can be used as performance security toward logistics clients.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright deliverable forwards (tenor up to 24 months) with genuine commercial exposure
EUR/USD FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-floating, EUR-USD) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible or restricted currencies (e.g., NGN, EGP, PKR, EGP) covering SaaS dealer and telematics-vendor payment flows
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD FX options and collars with hedging intent, no speculative leverage and full board-approved FX policy documentation
FX forwards entered into with an eligible ECB-counterparty bank in Luxembourg, exempt from any exchange-authorisation regime

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Data Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des données au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary date of the initial RCS registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 500 for late filing; if overdue by more than 12 months, the RCS may initiate administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings against the partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation (Déclaration annuelle de confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the initial RBE registration; and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 for non-compliance; distribution of profits, management fees, or liquidation proceeds is legally blocked until the confirmation is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels) – applicable when the SCSp exceeds the small-enterprise thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Corporate Accounts Archive
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end (i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year entity).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines ranging from EUR 1,000 to EUR 10,000; persistent non-filing can lead to administrative strike-off and civil liability of the general partner for damages sustained by third parties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total > EUR 5,500,000; net turnover > EUR 11,000,000; average number of employees > 50. A mandatory audit also applies if the SCSp is a regulated CSSF entity or constitutes an alternative investment fund regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register, accounting and annual accounts, as amended (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU). IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts and voluntarily for certain unconsolidated filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file initial beneficial ownership details with the RBE within one month of registration, then reconfirm the accuracy of the filed data each year within 30 days following the anniversary of the RBE registration. Any transfer of interest or change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of that event. Non-confirmation triggers prohibition on any distributions to partners and carries criminal penalties.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City; reduced 15% CIT on taxable profits up to EUR 175,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent; no entity-level CIT. Partners may claim: 80% IP Box exemption for qualifying logistics/route-optimization IP, 100% participation exemption on dividends/capital gains, investment tax credit (up to 12% on intangibles), and interest deduction on qualifying equity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 630 – Luxembourg Partnership Income Allocation Return (via MyGuichet.lu electronic filing)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year closed (e.g., FY2023 return due 31 December 2024)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, RCS number and registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter name and RCS number exactly as shown on the Trade and Companies Register; non-resident general partner must appoint a Luxembourg process agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership status and tax transparency election
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm under Article 164 LIR that no election has been made to treat the SCSp as taxable and that all partners are known.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross commercial profit (or loss) of the taxable year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State net result after depreciation; allocate non-resident partners' share separately.
Add back taxes on income (CIT, ICC), representation costs at 50%, fines, and withholding taxes recharged.
This is the SCSp-level taxable income that will be split among partners in accordance with their agreed profit shares; not remitted to partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation to general and limited partners (name, tax ID, residence)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide each partner's name, country of residence, participation percentage, and allocated income; non-resident partners must prove eligibility under a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of any business income subject to municipal business tax (ICC)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the municipality where activities are carried out; mark 'nil' for passive holding/financing activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: default tax assessment and 10% surcharge plus monthly interest of 0.6%; false declaration: fine up to EUR 50,000 (Article 175 LIR) and imprisonment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 700 – Municipal Business Tax Declaration (ICC) (via Luxembourg City tax administration / MyGuichet)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the following calendar year (same as CIT return)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Luxembourg address of the activity; overseas back-office does not relieve SCSp of ICC exposure.
If the SCSp is transparent, take the Box 5 taxable income after CIT adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for trade tax (ICC) paid in prior year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allow for the 2% deduction of ICC itself (the so-called 'deduction for commercial business tax').

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rounding adjustment and tax base per municipality
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-check with the Lex500 city coefficient if business carried on in multiple communes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applied ICC rate from the commune's schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 6.75% standard Luxembourg City quotient; if business uses multiple offices, allocate by payroll/asset factors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For non-filing, an estimated ICC assessment plus annual interest at 0.6% per month is imposed; a negligence fine of up to 15% of the assessed tax may be charged.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; SCSp distributions are not legally 'dividends' due to tax transparency and are therefore not subject to WHT; if the general partner elects corporate taxation, 15% WHT would apply on distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To use a DTA, the non-resident limited partner must provide a valid tax residence certificate and, in the case of an underlying Luxembourg company, a 12-month holding declaration; the partner must file for a refund on Form 200-T within the filing period if 15% was withheld on any non-qualifying distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% Luxembourg WHT on outgoing royalties and interest under domestic law; no source tax on fees for the route-optimization software license; anti-abuse rules under GAAR (Article 166 LIR) can reclassify abusive payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border intercompany transactions per year and consolidated group sales above EUR 35,000,000; above these, a Local File must be kept. A Master File is required for groups with consolidated sales over EUR 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No specific Economic Substance Regulation in Luxembourg, but GAAR under Article 166 LIR and the OECD Principal Purpose Test (PPT) in DTAs require genuine activity. The SCSp must maintain matrix of decision-making, local ERP server, call-recording records for dispatch optimization, formal partnership resolutions, and a physically attended office; absence of these will invalidate treaty access and can cause the partnership to be treated as a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Shell Company (Artificial Transparent Structure)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp to route logistics SaaS income through Luxembourg while no Luxembourg substance, staff or decision-making exists, solely to extract treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp for tax purposes; re-characterization of profits as directly taxable in Luxembourg at partner level; penalty up to 25% of tax understated and monthly interest of 0.6%; criminal fine up to EUR 50,000 (Article 175 LIR).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner may be personally liable for any unpaid tax, surcharges and interest; travel ban and imprisonment up to 2 years in aggravated fraud.
